# requireNil

<link-summary>Returns the value as `null` or `undefined`, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNil() — Returns the value as `null` or `undefined`, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNil(
  value: unknown,
  message: string = "Expected null or undefined."
): null | undefined;
```

The absent values, and only those: `0`, `""` and `false` are present values and do not qualify.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :------------------------------------------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                  | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected null or undefined."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`null | undefined` — the same value, typed as `null` or `undefined`.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                               |
| :------------------------- | :-------------------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not `null` or `undefined`. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNil(null); // => null
requireNil(undefined); // => undefined
requireNil(0); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNil(""); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
